es: Distinguir en una noticia los hechos verificables, las afirmaciones sin prueba y las opiniones, y reconocer sus señales.

vocabulary.es: rumores, lo que se oye decir
al pie de la letra, sin cuestionarlo

teaching.en: Anything presented as a verifiable fact should pass a simple test: can an independent reader verify it in a public record?
teaching.es: Todo lo que se presenta como un hecho comprobable debería superar una prueba sencilla: ¿puede un lector independiente verificarlo en un registro público?
teaching.explanationEs: Verify es el verbo de la comprobación; un hecho se apoya en un registro, no en quien lo cuenta.
segments: Anything presented as a verifiable fact should pass a simple test:
can an independent reader verify it in a public record?
teaching.audioText: Anything presented as a verifiable fact should pass a simple test: can an independent reader verify it in a public record?

teaching.en: The report says the minister allegedly accepted gifts, which remains an unsupported claim until someone produces hard evidence.
teaching.es: El informe dice que el ministro supuestamente aceptó regalos, lo que sigue siendo una afirmación sin respaldo hasta que alguien presente pruebas sólidas.
teaching.explanationEs: Allegedly avisa de que nadie ha demostrado lo que sigue; hard evidence es incontable.
segments: The report says the minister allegedly accepted gifts, which
remains an unsupported claim until someone produces hard evidence.
teaching.audioText: The report says the minister allegedly accepted gifts, which remains an unsupported claim until someone produces hard evidence.

teaching.en: A witness who repeats what a neighbour said is offering hearsay, and an anonymous source who cannot be named deserves extra caution.
teaching.es: Un testigo que repite lo que dijo un vecino ofrece rumores, y una fuente anónima que no puede nombrarse merece aún más cautela.
teaching.explanationEs: Hearsay es incontable: no lleva artículo ni plural.
segments: A witness who repeats what a neighbour said is offering hearsay,
and an anonymous source who cannot be named deserves extra caution.
teaching.audioText: A witness who repeats what a neighbour said is offering hearsay, and an anonymous source who cannot be named deserves extra caution.

teaching.en: Whether the new stadium is ugly is a matter of opinion, so no record or measurement could ever verify it.
teaching.es: Que el nuevo estadio sea feo es cuestión de opinión, así que ningún registro ni medición podría verificarlo jamás.
teaching.explanationEs: Un juicio de gusto no se comprueba: es a matter of opinion.
segments: Whether the new stadium is ugly is a matter of
opinion, so no record or measurement could ever verify it.
teaching.audioText: Whether the new stadium is ugly is a matter of opinion, so no record or measurement could ever verify it.

teaching.en: An official statement that publishes its official figures is stronger than a rumour that allegedly comes from someone inside the ministry.
teaching.es: Un comunicado oficial que publica sus cifras oficiales es más sólido que un rumor que supuestamente viene de alguien del ministerio.
teaching.explanationEs: Official statement y official figures permiten que cualquiera compruebe el dato.
segments: An official statement that publishes its official figures is stronger than
a rumour that allegedly comes from someone inside the ministry.
teaching.audioText: An official statement that publishes its official figures is stronger than a rumour that allegedly comes from someone inside the ministry.

teaching.en: A sensational headline tempts readers to accept the story at face value, yet a careful reader will verify the key detail before sharing it.
teaching.es: Un titular sensacionalista tienta a los lectores a aceptar la noticia sin cuestionarla, pero un lector cuidadoso verificará el dato clave antes de compartirla.
teaching.explanationEs: At face value = tal como se presenta, sin comprobarlo.
segments: A sensational headline tempts readers to accept the story at face value,
yet a careful reader will verify the key detail before sharing it.
teaching.audioText: A sensational headline tempts readers to accept the story at face value, yet a careful reader will verify the key detail before sharing it.

prompt.es: ¿Qué parte del texto es un hecho comprobable y no una opinión?

choices.text: That the bridge is the ugliest structure in the whole region.
That most residents privately agree with the local blogger.
That the bridge opened in 1998 and cost 2.3 million pounds.

feedback.es: Solo la fecha y el coste figuran en un comunicado que cualquiera puede consultar; lo demás es un juicio de gusto y una suposición sobre otros.

hint.es: Busca el dato que cualquiera podría comprobar en un documento oficial.

origin.text: The town council's press release states that the bridge opened on 4 May 1998 and cost 2.3 million pounds. A local blogger, however, calls it the ugliest structure in the region and claims that most residents privately agree with him.

prompt.es: Completa: «El vídeo supuestamente muestra al alcalde saliendo antes de la reunión.»

feedback.es: Allegedly señala que lo que muestra el vídeo aún no está demostrado; la frase siguiente confirma que falta la grabación completa.

hint.es: Adverbio que avisa de que nadie lo ha comprobado todavía.

origin.text: A post is circulating online. The video ___ shows the mayor leaving the meeting early, but nobody has produced the full recording.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Un lector atento verificará el dato de forma independiente antes de compartirlo.»

answer.text: A careful reader will verify the detail independently before sharing it
accepted: A careful reader will verify the detail independently before sharing it
Before sharing it a careful reader will verify the detail independently
A careful reader will independently verify the detail before sharing it
Before sharing it a careful reader will independently verify the detail

feedback.es: El adverbio independently cierra la oración principal y before sharing it introduce el momento de la comprobación.

hint.es: Sujeto + will + verify; el adverbio de modo va después del complemento.

prompt.es: ¿Qué actitud adopta la autora ante la promesa del titular?

choices.text: She doubts it, since the company itself gives no firm numbers.
She accepts it as a forecast, although the company sounds cautious.
She doubts it, since the company has a history of broken promises.
She welcomes it, but wants an official statement to follow soon.

feedback.es: Trata la promesa como «unsupported claim»: la propia empresa solo habla de una reducción posible y no da cifras.

origin.text: The headline promises that the new ferry will cut commuting times in half. Yet the company's own statement speaks only of a possible reduction and offers no official figures, so I would treat the promise as an unsupported claim rather than a forecast.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué la locutora no da la noticia por cierta.

choices.text: The story comes from a colleague who is known to invent news.
The story has passed through several people and lacks official confirmation.
The story has been denied in an official statement from the company.
The story is only her own opinion about the plant's future.

feedback.es: La noticia ha pasado por tres personas y no hay comunicado oficial; la locutora no acusa a nadie de mentir.

origin.audio: My colleague insists that the plant will close in June. When I asked how she knew, she admitted that a driver had mentioned it, and he had heard it from someone in the canteen. That is hearsay, passed along three times. Until the company issues an official statement, I will not take it at face value.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con el tipo de enunciado que representa.

pairs: The scheme has been a disaster.
An insider allegedly leaked the plan.
A friend of a friend told me.

feedback.es: Cada frase encaja en un tipo distinto: dato de registro, juicio, afirmación sin pruebas y rumor.

pairs: The scheme has been a disaster.
An insider allegedly leaked the plan.
A friend of a friend told me.

prompt.es: Escucha el pódcast y elige lo que la locutora da a entender sobre la noticia.

choices.text: The plant will almost certainly close, whatever the company says in public.
The website invented its anonymous source to attract more readers.
Repeating an unverified headline can turn a rumour into accepted fact.
Companies should never comment on rumours about their own plans.

feedback.es: La locutora admite que el rumor podría ser cierto, pero critica que se presentara como hecho y se repitiera sin comprobar: así «a worry becomes a fact».

origin.audio: Last week a local website ran a story under the headline Plant to Close, Hundreds to Lose Jobs. Within hours it had been shared thousands of times. I phoned the company, and a spokesperson told me that no decision had been taken and that an official statement would follow on Friday. The website's only source was an anonymous message posted by someone who claimed to work there. Of course, the rumour may turn out to be true. But the writer presented a possibility as a verifiable fact, and readers who took the headline at face value went on to repeat it. That, in my view, is how a worry becomes a fact.

prompt.es: ¿Qué enunciado del informe es una afirmación sin pruebas y no un hecho ni una opinión?

choices.text: That 62 per cent of commuters now take the bus.
That the new timetable is the best thing in years.
That the survey included 400 commuters.
That congestion has fallen by half.

feedback.es: Se dice que el municipio tiene pruebas de la bajada, pero no las ha publicado: es una afirmación sin respaldo. El porcentaje y la muestra son datos; «the best» es opinión.

origin.text: The survey of 400 commuters, published in March, found that 62 per cent now take the bus. The report adds that the new timetable is the best thing to happen to the city in years, and the mayor's office allegedly has proof that congestion has fallen by half, although it has not released it.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es una afirmación sin respaldo, no un hallazgo.»

feedback.es: Sin ensayo ni médico citado, el folleto solo ofrece una afirmación sin respaldo: unsupported claim es la colocación habitual.

origin.text: The leaflet insists that its special tea prevents colds in a day. It quotes no trial and names no doctor, so it amounts to an unsupported ___ rather than a finding.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La fuente anónima ofreció rumores en lugar de pruebas sólidas.»

answer.text: The anonymous source offered hearsay rather than hard evidence
accepted: The anonymous source offered hearsay rather than hard evidence
Rather than hard evidence the anonymous source offered hearsay

feedback.es: Rather than contrapone dos cosas: lo que la fuente ofreció (hearsay) y lo que debería haber ofrecido (hard evidence).

prompt.es: ¿Qué pretende la editora con su comentario sobre el tercer párrafo?

choices.text: To persuade him to tone down a conclusion his figures do not fully support.
To warn him that the provisional report may soon be replaced by a final one.
To accuse him of copying the provisional report without checking it.
To tell him that the official statement proves the scheme worked.

feedback.es: Le pide una formulación más cautelosa porque la conclusión es más fuerte que los datos; no le pide borrar nada ni le acusa de copiar.

origin.text: Dear Tom, thank you for the draft. Before it goes online, please look again at the third paragraph. You wrote that the scheme has been a total failure, yet the only figures you quote come from a provisional report, and the official statement is not out. I would prefer a wording such as appears to have fallen short. Regards, Mia.

prompt.es: Escribe una frase que presente la noticia como afirmación sin pruebas.

answer.text: The post claims that the new bus route cuts journey times in half, but it offers no hard evidence and quotes no official figures.
accepted: The post claims that the new bus route cuts journey times in half, but it offers no hard evidence and quotes no official figures.
The post allegedly proves that the new bus route cuts journey times in half, yet it gives no hard evidence and no official figures.
The website claims that the new route cuts the journey time in half, but it provides no hard evidence and quotes no official figures.

feedback.es: Una afirmación sin respaldo se señala con claims that o allegedly y con la ausencia de hard evidence y de cifras oficiales.

origin.text: La publicación dice que la nueva ruta de autobús reduce a la mitad el tiempo de viaje, pero no aporta pruebas sólidas ni cifras oficiales.

prompt.es: Completa: «Demasiados lectores se creen cualquier titular sensacionalista sin más.»

feedback.es: At face value se combina con take, accept o read: aceptar algo tal como se presenta, sin cuestionarlo.

origin.text: Many readers never ask who wrote a story. Too many of them ___ every sensational headline at face value, and that is how rumours spread.
